title: Children as Props Re-render Isolator
concept: Children Prop Reference Stability Across Parent Re-renders
problemStatement: Implement `simulateChildrenPattern(parentRenders, childElement)` that tracks how many times `childElement` is re-created when its parent container re-renders 5 times.
interviewTrap: This is one of Dan Abramov's most famous React mental models: 'Before You memo()', try moving state down or lifting content up.

testCases.name: Preserves identical child reference across parent renders
testCases.testFn: const child = { type: 'ExpensiveTree' }; return simulateChildrenPattern(5, child).allIdentical;

testCases.name: Maintains render count

details.name: Preserves identical child reference across parent renders

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Passing an expensive component as the `children` prop `<Parent><ExpensiveTree /></Parent>` prevents `ExpensiveTree` from re-rendering when `Parent`'s state changes! Because `ExpensiveTree` is evaluated in the grandparent's render scope, its element reference is identical across `Parent` re-renders.
